disease_label_per_paper: Anti-LGI1 encephalitis causing faciobrachial dystonic seizures
presentation_summary: 69-year-old man had six months of vague symptoms and a three-month history of abnormal spasms affecting the left face, arm, and leg, sometimes right-sided.
The spasms lasted about a second, occurred every few minutes through the day, and were considered compatible with faciobrachial dystonic seizures.
He had subtle cognitive impairment, daytime somnolence, insomnia, and 4 kg weight loss, but no fever, rash, cough, hallucinations, delusions, or bleeding.
Cognition was slightly reduced on testing with ACE-R 93/100 and MMSE 29/30.
Blood tests showed SIADH-like hyponatremia: serum sodium 126 mmol/L, serum osmolality 267 mOsm/kg H2O, urine osmolality 764 mmol/kg H2O, and urine sodium 106 mmol/L.
VGKC antibodies were strongly positive at 1002 pM and LGI1 antibodies were positive; CASPR2, NMDAR, GAD, amphiphysin, glycine receptor, and basal ganglia/neuronal antibodies were negative.
CSF was acellular with normal biochemistry, no bacterial growth, no oligoclonal bands, and normal opening pressure.
Two EEGs did not show epileptiform discharges.
MRI brain showed left medial temporal lobe/hippocampal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity and mild asymmetrical enlargement without mass effect or hemorrhage.

Initial IVIG and oral prednisolone were insufficient; later plasma exchange followed by high-dose IV methylprednisolone produced very good effect, and he had no relapse during three years of follow-up.
